analysis_steps.goal: Subtract dust continuum from MIRI MRS spectrum

method.value: Estimate dust continuum using a Savitzky-Golay filter with a third-order polynomial via pybaselines, iteratively mask emission lines above 2 sigma, subtract continuum, and mask remaining 3 sigma downward spikes.

evidence.quote: In short, the adopted method estimates the dust continuum emission using the `pybaselines` package (cite: Erb_2022). As a first step, a dust continuum level is guessed using a Savitzky-Golay filter with a third order polynomial.

Then, all emission lines extending above $2\sigma$ of the standard deviation are masked. Once no emission lines are left, the dust continuum is determined and subtracted. The last step of this procedure consists of masking the remaining $3\sigma$ downward spikes.

findings_qualitative.value: The inner disk of J0438 is O-dominated (H2O, CO2, HCN, H2, [Ar+], [Ne+]) and lacks abundant hydrocarbons except for C2H2, resembling T Tauri disks with C/O < 1 rather than typical hydrocarbon-rich VLMS/BD disks.

evidence.quote: The JWST MIRI-MRS spectrum of J0438 resembles that of a disk around a T Tauri star with a C/O ratio below unity. The volatile reservoir is O-dominated, composed of H$_2$O, CO$_2$ and, contrarily to most VLMS and BD disks investigated so far, of only one hydrocarbon (i.e., C$_2$H$_2$).

findings_qualitative.value: J0438 exhibits mid-IR seesaw continuum variability (pivot at ~11.5 um, 30% weaker at 6 um and 15% stronger at 20 um over 16 years) as well as line variability in [Ne+], H2, and H2O.

evidence.quote: The largest offsets are found between the MIRI (2023-10-01) and the low-resolution IRS observations (2007-10-07) taken 16 years apart with the MIRI spectrum roughly $30\%$ weaker at $6~ \mu$m and $15\%$ stronger at $20~\mu$m.
The mid-IR variability of J0438 can be ascribed to a seesaw behaviour where the pivot point is at $\lambda\simeq11.5\,\mu$m.

findings_qualitative.value: Marginally extended emission is detected in JWST-MIRI MRS for H2 S(1), S(3), S(5) and [Ne+], tracing a disk wind and/or disk surface rather than a collimated jet.

evidence.quote: The inspection of the JWST data cubes shows marginally extended emission for the H$_2 \, \, S$(1), $S$(3) and $S$(5) lines, as well as of [Ne$^{+}$], for the first time in a BD disk.
Interestingly, the emission patterns of H$_2$ and [Ne$^{+}$] are similar and are not attributable to a jet, but plausibly to a disk wind and/or to the disk surface.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA Band 7 reveals non-bipolar extended CO (J=3-2) emission up to 420 au with low velocity dispersion (±2 km/s), and HST/ACS detects a faint point source 0.49'' E, 0.86'' S that is not detected in ALMA dust continuum.

evidence.quote: The red-shifted NE lobe extends up to approximately 280 au whereas the blue-shifted emission spans up to $420~$au. The SE lobe appears to be disconnected from the central object possibly due to the presence of an interfering planetary-mass companion robustly detected with a S/N $>5$ in the HST/ACS images but not observed in the ALMA dust continuum maps (Fig. 6).

claims.hypothesis: The inner disk of the M7.25 brown dwarf J0438 has a hydrocarbon-rich chemistry typical of very low-mass stars and brown dwarfs.
claims.experiment: Observed J0438 with JWST-MIRI MRS (4.9-28 um), performed simultaneous LTE slab modeling of molecular emission (13.4-18 um), and compared molecular line flux ratios (C2H2/H2O, HCN/H2O, CO2/H2O) to VLMS and T Tauri samples.
claims.result: Detected H2O, CO2, HCN, H2, [Ar+], [Ne+], and only C2H2 among hydrocarbons (no CH4, C2H4, C2H6, C3H4, C4H2, C6H6); measured lower CO2/H2O, HCN/H2O, and C2H2/H2O flux ratios than other late M-star disks.
claims.finding: Refuted: J0438 lacks abundant hydrocarbons and instead has an O-dominated volatile reservoir (C/O < 1) resembling earlier-type T Tauri disks, representing an intermediate evolutionary stage slowly evolving out of a water-rich phase.

evidence.quote: Despite its late spectral type (M7.25), the spectrum of J0438 resembles those of inner disks around earlier-type stars (K1–M5, T Tauri stars), with a volatile reservoir lacking hydrocarbons (except for acetylene, C$_2$H$_2$) and dominated by water.

Additionally, J0438 appears to have consistently lower CO$_2$/H$_2$O, HCN/H$_2$O and C$_2$H$_2$/H$_2$O flux ratios with respect to disks around other late M-stars disks (e.g., J160532, ISO-ChaI 147, Sz 28; (cite: tabone2023; Arabhavi2024; Kanwar2024)).

claims.hypothesis: The high inclination (~70 deg) of the J0438 disk obscures the inner disk and causes the non-detection of hydrocarbons weaker than C2H2.
claims.experiment: Ran thermochemical disk models following Kanwar et al. (2025) varying the disk inclination from 45 deg to 70 deg.
claims.result: The peak flux density of C2H2 decreases by approximately 33% when inclination changes from i=45 deg to i=70 deg, remaining well within the MIRI detection limit.
claims.finding: The high disk inclination is not responsible for the non-detection of hydrocarbons weaker than C2H2; instead, young age (~0.6 Myr), low mass accretion rate, and a possible inner hole at 0.28 au preserve the water reservoir.

evidence.quote: We found that the peak flux density of C$_2$H$_2$ decreases of approximately $33\%$ when the disk inclination changes from *i*=45$^{\circ}$ to *i*=70$^{\circ}$, which is well within our detection limit. This result made us confident that the inclination of our BD disk ($67^{\circ}-71^{\circ}$) is not responsible for the non-detection of hydrocarbons weaker than C$_2$H$_2$.

claims.hypothesis: J0438 is a dynamic system experiencing inner disk structural changes and extended outflowing or infalling gas activity.
claims.experiment: Compared the 2023 JWST-MIRI MRS spectrum with 2007/2009 Spitzer-IRS spectra, extracted PSF-subtracted moment 0 maps from MIRI datacubes, deconvolved archival HST/ACS F814W images, and analyzed archival ALMA Band 7 CO (J=3-2) observations.
claims.result: Found seesaw mid-IR continuum variability pivoting at ~11.5 um and [Ne+] line flux 2.5x brighter than in 2009; marginally extended H2 S(1), S(3), S(5) and [Ne+] emission in MIRI; and non-bipolar extended CO (J=3-2) emission up to 420 au with velocity dispersion ±2 km/s in ALMA.
claims.finding: J0438 is highly dynamic, with inner disk dynamical changes driving seesaw variability, a disk wind/surface traced by H2 and [Ne+], and large-scale extended CO emission potentially related to a late-infall event or binary/companion interaction.

evidence.quote: The mid-IR variability of J0438 can be ascribed to a seesaw behaviour where the pivot point is at $\lambda\simeq11.5\,\mu$m.

ALMA Band 7 observations show extended CO ($J=3-2$) emission spanning up to $420~$au from the brown dwarf with a velocity dispersion of $\pm 2$ km s$^{-1}$, perpendicular to the line of sight. The low CO velocities and the lack of a bipolar pattern makes it challenging to attribute the extended emission to an outflow. A late-infall event cannot be ruled out at this stage without dedicated modelling.

why_this_data.value: J0438 is one of the very few highly inclined (~70 deg) brown dwarf disks known, has the most complete SED for a brown dwarf disk, and high-resolution JWST-MIRI MRS spectra paired with HST and ALMA allow characterization of both its inner disk chemistry and extended dynamical activity.

evidence.quote: Interestingly, among all VLMS and BD disks targeted in JWST-MIRI Cycles 1 and 2 so far ($\sim$ 25) all of them appear to have a close to face-on configuration except for the target of this work.

Thanks to the high spectral resolving power of JWST-MIRI MRS ($R\!\sim\!3000$; (cite: Labiano2021)) we confirm the presence of faint water emission throughout the JWST mid-infrared (mid-IR) spectrum of J0438 as well as of a set of atomic, molecular and ionic emission lines

why_this_method.value: Automated continuum subtraction via pybaselines avoids bias from visual selection in line-rich spectra; simultaneous MCMC fitting of all six species avoids bias from sequential species subtraction; pair-wise dither subtraction reduces noise for faint sources.

evidence.quote: To subtract the background a direct pair-wise dither subtraction was carried out. This method is particularly suited for faint sources and guarantees the reduction of the noise level in the spectrum.

We followed the continuum subtraction procedure described in (cite: Temmink2024), instead of identifying line-free channels tracing the dust emission by eye. A visual selection of dust continuum points would inevitably result in an inaccurate continuum determination due to the line richness of the MIRI spectrum.

The slab modelling procedure consists of performing an Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC; (cite: Foreman-Mackey2013)) fit of all the six selected species simultaneously, instead of fitting iteratively one species at the time (i.e., subtracting the synthetic model of water first, then moving to the next species, and so on). This procedure has the advantage of reducing the bias introduced by the sequential subtraction of different synthetic spectra

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Spectrophotometric calibration uncertainties or aperture size differences between Spitzer-IRS and JWST-MIRI as the cause of the mid-IR continuum offset (rejected because offsets exceed calibration uncertainties and reverse sign around 11.5 um).

evidence.quote: The reported spectrophotometric accuracy is 2–10% for SST-IRS (cite: Furlan2006; Watson2009) and $5.6 \pm 0.7\%$ for JWST-MIRI MRS (cite: Argyriou2023), which confidently rules out calibration uncertainties, especially for the shorter wavelengths.

However, this pattern is not observed for the full spectral coverage and instead, the MIRI spectrum is consistently stronger longwards of $12\, \mu$m, supporting the presence of both continuum and line variability (see also Appendix 9).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: High disk inclination (~70 deg) causing the non-detection of hydrocarbons weaker than C2H2 (rejected via thermochemical modeling showing only a ~33% drop in C2H2 peak flux density).

evidence.quote: We found that the peak flux density of C$_2$H$_2$ decreases of approximately $33\%$ when the disk inclination changes from *i*=45$^{\circ}$ to *i*=70$^{\circ}$, which is well within our detection limit. This result made us confident that the inclination of our BD disk ($67^{\circ}-71^{\circ}$) is not responsible for the non-detection of hydrocarbons weaker than C$_2$H$_2$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Visual selection of line-free continuum channels and sequential one-by-one slab fitting of molecular species (rejected in favor of automated pybaselines continuum subtraction and simultaneous 6-species MCMC fitting).

limitations_admitted.value: 0D LTE slab models do not account for the multi-dimensional physical structure of the disk, so R only represents an equivalent emitting area radius; C2H2 exhibits a degeneracy between column density and emitting radius, CO2 column density is only a lower limit due to limited S/N, and OH and 13CO2 are poorly constrained.

evidence.quote: Note that $R$ should not be ascribed to a radius within the disk as the adopted models do not take into account the multi-dimensional physical structure of the disk.
Deviations from this behavior are seen for C$_2$H$_2$ ($N\!\sim\!10^{13}~$cm$^{-2}$ and $R\!\sim~0.9~$au), reporting a degeneracy between the column density and the emitting radius.
Due to the limited S/N, the column density of CO$_2$ remained challenging to constrain, and the current best slab is limited to a maximum column density of $10^{17}$cm$^{-2}$.

limitations_admitted.value: Slab modeling is restricted to 13.4-18 um because shorter wavelengths are affected by photospheric absorption and silicate bands, and wavelengths beyond 18 um have considerably higher noise.

evidence.quote: We did not produce synthetic spectra for the region below $13.4~\mu$m as it is largely dominated by the absorption lines from the central object up until $7.3~\mu$m (e.g., (cite: Li2024); Fig. 10) and by the silicate band in absorption and emission (Fig. 9). Beyond 18 $\mu$m, the noise level increases considerably, therefore we restrict the slab modelling analysis to wavelengths shorter than this.

limitations_admitted.value: Current observations cannot distinguish whether the HST/ACS point source is a background field star or a planetary-mass companion, nor whether the ALMA extended CO emission is an outflow, binary interaction, or late-infall event without dedicated modeling and follow-up.

evidence.quote: With our current data is not possible to disentangle whether this is a field star or a planetary-mass companion and further work is required to confirm its nature.

The low CO velocities and the lack of a bipolar pattern makes it challenging to attribute the extended emission to an outflow. A late-infall event cannot be ruled out at this stage without dedicated modelling.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA Band 7 data reduction and imaging parameters (velocity channel ranges for red/blue lobes, noise levels, contour thresholds in Fig. 6) are not specified in this paper and rely entirely on earlier works.
The PSF subtraction method used for the JWST-MIRI MRS extended emission maps relies on an unpublished paper (Kurtovic et al. in prep.).
